land.text: Turov and Haradok, still ruled by Rurikids when the principality joined Lithuania

predecessors.note: The Turov-and-Pinsk dossier (eu-16-e) closes on 1293; Cliopatria's separate Turov row starts in 1294. Same page, Wikidata Q671362.

land.text: Turov, which 'non-violently joined the Grand Duchy' in the early 14th century

successors.note: The Grand Duchy's dossier (eu-15) records the gain in 1326, the first year of Cliopatria's Lithuanian shape that holds Turov (127 of 127 cells).

keyframe_review.note: 28,994 km2 (125 cells), 27.2-30.6 E, 51.3-53.3 N, the eastern half of the old Turov-Pinsk land along the Pripyat. The page gives only 'the territory of modern-day Belarus and northern Ukraine' and no area; the Turov city (27.75 E) is inside the shape. Unverified beyond that: the page names no frontier.

29,467 km2 (127 cells, two more than 1294) for 1314-1325. The page dates no event of these years; it says only 'In the early 14th century the Principality non-violently joined the Grand Duchy', so the shape's end in 1325 is Cliopatria's.

region.text: Turov and Haradok, the eastern part of the old Turov-Pinsk land

ledger.note: 1294 (Cliopatria's first year): Turov appears as its own principality, the Pinsk part having split off as a semi-independent appanage. The page has 'Dmitry Yuryevich (1292-)' among the princes and no founding event; 'the Principality became more and more divided between several sons of the duke Yury'.

1325 (last year of Cliopatria's shape): Turov joins the Grand Duchy of Lithuania. 'In the early 14th century the Principality non-violently joined the Grand Duchy' and the infobox 'Incorporation into the Grand Duchy of Lithuania: 14th century'; the page gives no year (Gediminas '(1320- ?)' appears in the princes' list). The eu-15 Grand Duchy dossier records the gain in 1326.
The principality ends as a state; its land goes to the Grand Duchy of Lithuania. The year is Cliopatria's.

certainty.note: No page gives a boundary; the Pripyat marsh frontier with Pinsk, Minsk and Galicia-Volhynia is approximate.

sources.title: Principality of Turov
sources.note: The only page opened for this state: capital, early 14th-century incorporation into Lithuania, princes, sub-principalities. Thin: it dates no event of 1294-1325.

notes: SEPARATE FROM PINSK. Cliopatria's Turov row (1294-1325) and Pinsk row share Wikidata Q671362 with the earlier 'Principality of Turov and Pinsk' (eu-16-e dossier, 1188-1293); here Turov is its own state because the page has Pinsk as a semi-independent appanage already ruled by a Gediminid (Narymunt) while 'Turov and Haradok were still ruled by Rurikids'; see principality-of-pinsk. NO DATES: the single page gives no year for Turov's incorporation into Lithuania ('early 14th century'; infobox '14th century'), so the end 1325 and the start 1294 are Cliopatria's years (events at confidence 1); the Grand Duchy of Lithuania dossier (eu-15) records the gain in 1326 with a note that the dates of the conquests are 'impossible to follow'. A second page (Gediminas, Lithuanian chronicle, or the Turov-Pinsk articles in other languages) would be needed. Page budget: one page of 1-2.
